jurisdiction: England, Wales and Northern Ireland (JCQ awarding bodies AQA, Pearson Edexcel, Cambridge OCR, WJEC/Eduqas) for timetables and deadlines; Scotland (Qualifications Scotland, formerly SQA) for the results day only. CCEA (Northern Ireland) timetables and deadlines are not covered.
refreshRule: Calendar-driven (cadenceDays null). Re-verify (a) when JCQ publishes the June 2028 key dates and the boards their final summer 2028 timetables (provisional for consultation in February, final in early May — AQA, Pearson, OCR and WJEC all published summer 2027 finals by July 2026), (b) when the November 2027 GCSE series key dates appear (September), (c) on any Ofqual/DfE announcement of a reformed GCSE or A level specification or accreditation, and (d) on 2027-01-15 regardless, when this file flips to due.
verificationMethod: Every date was read on verifiedDate from the document named in its source: the JCQ key-dates PDFs (June 2027, June 2026, November 2026) and timetable commentary, each board's own final timetable PDF (summer 2027, summer 2026 where still online, November 2026), each board's 2026/27 fees or key-dates document, the Qualifications Scotland results pages, and the DfE/Ofqual/board announcement pages for specification changes. `quote` reproduces the timetable row or sentence (columns collapsed to three spaces); `document` names the PDF and version. `previous` is the summer-2026 equivalent read from the board's own 2026 document — absent where that document is no longer served (Pearson's summer 2026 PDFs returned "Page not found" on 2026-10-04) or where there is no equivalent (November series). Pearson paper dates for 2027 therefore carry no `previous`. jcq.org.uk returns HTTP 403 to non-browser user agents; its PDFs were read through a browser-class fetch. Figures are read from the page, never from memory.
licence: The dates are facts; each is quoted in one line with attribution from documents that remain their publishers' copyright and are not reproduced further: "©JCQCIC 2026" (JCQ key-dates PDFs), "Copyright © 2026 AQA and its licensors. All rights reserved." (AQA timetables and fees), "© Pearson 2026" (Pearson key dates and fees), "© Cambridge OCR 2026" (OCR timetables), "© WJEC CBAC Ltd" (WJEC/Eduqas timetables and fees), Qualifications Scotland pages; gov.uk pages (DfE, Ofqual) are Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

timetable.title: Summer 2027 exam timetable — JCQ common window (10 May – 22 June 2027, contingency 23 June) and, per board, the dates of GCSE Maths, English Language and Combined Science papers and A-level Maths; all four boards' timetables are FINAL
timetable.note: Status on 2026-10-04: AQA ("The timetables on this page are definitive", GCSE v1.1, A-level v1.2), Pearson Edexcel ("Summer 2027 Examination Timetable - FINAL"), Cambridge OCR ("Final Examination Timetable June 2027") and WJEC/Eduqas ("FINAL Examination Timetable (version 2)") have all published final summer 2027 timetables; no board is still provisional. Exams sit in JCQ common slots, so the same paper falls on the same day at every board. Sessions start 09:00 (am) or 13:30 (pm). WJEC/Eduqas timetables no GCSE Combined Science (Eduqas offers separate sciences; Wales sits Science (Double Award) and, from 2027, The Sciences (Double Award)) and no Eduqas A level Mathematics.

spec-changes.title: Specification changes announced — first-teaching and first-exam years for new or revised GCSE/A-level specifications, the DfE reform timetable and Ofqual decisions
spec-changes.note: Status on 2026-10-04: no reformed (post-Curriculum-and-Assessment-Review) GCSE or A level specification exists yet; the DfE timetable is first teaching 2029/2030 (GCSE) and 2031/2032 (A level). The board-level changes listed are the accredited or announced new/amended specifications found on the boards' own update pages: AQA A-level Business (teaching from September 2026), Pearson A level History amendments (September 2026), OCR A Level Psychology H569 (September 2027), and Wales' Made-for-Wales GCSEs (first awards 2027). GCSE BSL has Ofqual rules but no accredited specification. Items absent here were not found on an official page, not ruled out.

figures.document: DfE, Curriculum and Assessment Review Final Report: government response (published 5 November 2025; PDF "Government response to the Curriculum and Assessment Review", November 2025)
figures.quote: Our aim is that some are ready for first teaching in 2029 and the rest for first teaching in 2030. … We will also seek to update corresponding AS and A levels to be ready for first teaching in 2031 and 2032, as the cohort progresses to 16 - 19.

previous.note: first appearance: no earlier announcement is recorded

figures.note: No reformed GCSE or A level specification or spec code exists yet; current specifications continue for every exam series through at least summer 2030 (GCSE) and 2032 (A level), plus resits.
